adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a shared helper `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, but it returns an unnormalized provider response (either a `fetch` Response from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` or whatever the provider refresh function returns). Call sites still implement their own “response → credential.key” mapping and parsing in divergent ways (e.g., GoogleCalendarService manually copies `token.access_token`/`expiry_date` then separately calls `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)`; Office365CalendarService parses JSON then calls `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, schema)`; some integrations just pass through the refresh result). Salesforce’s refresh path in `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts` bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens` entirely and implements its own refresh+persist flow. This supports the finding’s core point that the new sync mechanism doesn’t enforce a single normalized `{access_token, expiry_date, refresh_token?}` contract across apps, making drift/fragility a real, diff-grounded concern, even if the claim that “sync was wrong in each” can’t be verified from the diff alone.
